name: libfishsound
desc: Decode and encode audio data using the Xiph.org codecs
why: Xiph audio codec library, a close call since it is plumbing unless paired with a tool that makes the codecs interesting.

brief.what_it_is: libfishsound is a C programming library that decodes and encodes audio using the Xiph.org codecs, namely FLAC, Speex and Vorbis. It is a wrapper around the existing codec libraries that gives them one consistent, higher-level programming interface. It takes raw codec streams from a lower layer, such as UDP datagrams, and produces decoded audio or encoded streams. It has no direct dependency on Ogg; it is most often paired with liboggz when the codecs sit inside Ogg files. The page describes it as a library for developers, not an end-user tool.
brief.why_it_exists: The page frames it as a simple, consistent programming interface over the Xiph.org codecs, designed for use in a wide variety of applications. It is meant to be the layer between a codec and an application, without tying the application to Ogg containers.
brief.how_it_works: Developers call the libfishsound API to hand it raw codec packets, such as UDP datagrams, and get decoded audio back, or to feed audio in and get encoded codec streams out. Internally it wraps the existing FLAC, Speex and Vorbis libraries behind one interface. When the codecs are in files, Ogg encapsulation is handled by a separate layer such as liboggz.

brief.install_notes: Install from the 1.0.1 source tarball (libfishsound-1.0.1.tar.gz, about 650 KB, dated Feb 15 2025) or from the git repository. A full build depends on the Vorbis and Speex libraries. The page says it builds on GNU/Linux, Darwin/macOS and Win32, and other Unix-like systems should work via GNU autoconf. Windows builds use nmake Makefiles, Visual Studio .NET 2003 solution files, or Visual C++ 6.0 workspace files, all included in the source distribution. The page does not mention a Homebrew formula or the brew install command itself.
brief.standout: The library is built for raw codec streams that arrive without a container, such as UDP datagrams, rather than only for files. It handles FLAC, Speex and Vorbis behind one API, which makes it a fairly plain wrapper, so it is plumbing rather than a visible tool.
brief.status: quiet. The only dated item on the page is the 1.0.1 tarball from Feb 15 2025. The footer copyright reads 1994 - 2016, and the GitHub copy is marked obsolete, pointing to GitLab. I did not check commit history, so this is a judgment from the page alone.
brief.caveats: It is a library with no executables, so there is nothing to run directly from the command line. A full build needs the Vorbis and Speex libraries. The page lists FLAC, Speex and Vorbis only, though the site navigation also lists Opus. Windows support relies on older Visual Studio project files. The API documentation and examples are inside the source tarball and linked online, and I did not open them. The scout note calls it a close call since it is plumbing unless paired with a tool.
quotes: libfishsound provides a simple programming interface for decoding and encoding audio data using the Xiph.org codecs (FLAC, Speex and Vorbis).
libfishsound by itself is designed to handle raw codec streams from a lower level layer such as UDP datagrams.
libfishsound is a wrapper around the existing codec libraries and provides a consistent, higher-level programming interface.
